welcome.title: Welcome to visual-omp
welcome.body: Connect your providers and choose how omp works in your chats.

providers.title: Sign in to your providers
providers.body: Sign in to one or more providers. You can connect another before continuing.
providers.note: omp opens the sign-in process and stores your credentials. You can also use providers configured in your environment.

model.title: Choose your default model
model.body: Search configured models and save the model used for new chats.
model.emptyBody: Sign in to a provider to choose a model, or skip this step and configure one later in Settings.

permission.title: Choose your permission mode
permission.body: This sets the default for all projects. You can change it for each project later.

always-ask.title: Ask me first
always-ask.body: Ask before using tools, including edits and commands.

always-ask-cached.title: Ask and remember
always-ask-cached.body: Ask before using tools, with optional remembered file or folder approvals.

write.title: Edits OK
write.body: Allow reads and workspace edits. Ask before running commands and other execution tools.

yolo.title: Auto
yolo.body: Allow tools without asking. Commit or back up your work before using this mode.

appearance.title: Choose your appearance
appearance.body: Preview the app theme here. You can change it later in Settings.

done.title: You're all set
done.body: Your choices are saved. You can change them later in Settings.

missing.title: Install omp
missing.body: visual-omp is a desktop app for omp, the AI coding agent. omp isn't installed on this computer yet.

tooOld.title: Your omp is out of date
tooOld.body: visual-omp requires omp {{version}} or later. Update omp here to keep using your chats and settings.

refused.title: omp can't start
refused.body: omp is installed, but Windows didn't start it, and visual-omp needs omp for every chat.

step1.body: The installer is a single command, and its output appears in this window.
step1.bodyWindows: The installer is a single PowerShell command, and its output appears in this window.
step1.updateBody: visual-omp runs omp's own updater and shows its output in this window.
step1.managedUpdate: {{app}} manages this omp installation. Update omp in {{app}}, then choose Check for omp.
step1.copyHint: Copy the install command to run it yourself in a terminal.
step1.copyUpdateHint: Copy the update command to run it yourself in a terminal.
step1.copiedBody: Paste it into a terminal, then return and choose Check for omp.
step1.failed: The installer stopped with an error (code {{code}}). You can try again, or copy the command and run it yourself.

step2.title: Check for omp
step2.body: Once the installer finishes, check that visual-omp can find omp.
step2.bodyRefused: After you allow omp in Windows, check whether it starts.
step2.bodyUpdate: After updating, check that visual-omp can find a supported omp version.
step2.stillMissingBody: If you installed omp in a custom location, add its folder to PATH. Quit and reopen visual-omp, then choose Check for omp.

sidebar.title: Projects and chats
sidebar.body: The sidebar lists your projects and chats. Each request becomes a chat you can return to.

composer.title: Say what you want
composer.body: Type what you want in plain words and press Enter to send. Commands are optional shortcuts.

permission.title: How much omp does on its own
permission.body: This setting controls how much omp does before asking you. Auto lets omp edit files and run commands without approval, so commit or back up your work before you use it.

dock.title: Watch the work
dock.body: This panel shows changes, files, previews, outputs, running helpers, the plan and a terminal. Choose one from the menu at the top of the panel.

statusbar.title: Project and usage status
statusbar.body: The status bar shows git information, available plan usage and omp status. Open Usage & limits for estimated API cost.

help.title: Help
help.description: Short guides for common tasks and definitions of the terms visual-omp uses.
help.noMatchesBody: omp can answer questions about itself and about your project.
help.noMatchesLimited: Try other words, or open the omp documentation below.
help.askNeedsProjectBody: Questions open a new chat, and each chat belongs to a project folder.

more.title: More help
more.docsBody: Commands, settings and models for omp, on omp.sh.
more.reportBody: Opens the visual-omp issue list on GitHub, where you can describe what you did and what happened.

firstChat.title: Your first chat
firstChat.summary: Pick a folder, describe what you want, and watch omp work.
firstChat.s1: Open a project. A project is a folder on your computer that omp works in.
firstChat.s2: Start a new chat and describe what you want in plain words, the way you'd tell a colleague.
firstChat.s3: Watch omp work. Each step appears as a row you can expand for details, and the side panel shows files and changes as omp makes them.
firstChat.s4: Reply to refine the result. If you send a message while omp is busy, it waits in a queue until omp finishes.

autoMode.title: Staying safe with Auto mode
autoMode.summary: Choose how much omp may do before asking you.
autoMode.s1: The permission button under the message box sets how much omp does on its own: Ask me first, Edits OK, or Auto.
autoMode.s2: Auto lets omp edit files and run commands without asking for approval. Use it in projects you trust.
autoMode.s3: Want more control? Ask me first makes omp stop before every edit or command so you can approve it.
autoMode.s4: Commit or back up your work before using Auto. Rewinding changes the conversation; it doesn't guarantee that file changes or the effects of commands are undone.

rewind.title: Rewinding and forking
rewind.summary: Go back to an earlier point, or try another direction.
rewind.s1: Hover one of your messages to see Rewind and Fork.
rewind.s2: Rewind goes back to that point so you can say it differently. Messages after it stay in the branch tree.
rewind.s3: Fork copies the chat into a new one, so you can try a different idea without losing this one.
rewind.s4: The branch tree shows every rewind and fork as a map, so you can jump between versions.

questions.title: When omp asks questions
questions.summary: Answer omp's questions and approvals right in the chat.
questions.s1: Sometimes omp needs a decision from you, such as which option to pick or whether it may run something.
questions.s2: A question card appears in the chat, and the chat is marked in the sidebar so you don't miss it.
questions.s3: Select an option or type your own answer, then choose Send answer. omp continues once it has your answer.
questions.s4: If you're away, visual-omp shows a count on its Dock or taskbar icon when a chat needs your answer.

context.def: Everything omp can see at once: your messages, its replies, and the files it has read. It has a size limit.

token.def: A small chunk of text, about three-quarters of a word. Context size and cost are measured in tokens.

compaction.def: Summarizing the chat so far to free up room in the context, so the conversation can keep going.

planMode.def: omp thinks through an approach and shows you a plan to approve before it changes anything.

worktree.def: A separate copy of your project for one chat, so its changes stay apart from your main files.

mcp.def: A standard way to plug outside tools, like a database or ticket tracker, into omp.

agent.def: A reusable specialist omp can hand work to, like a reviewer or an explorer.

skill.def: An add-on set of instructions that teaches omp how to do a particular kind of task.

hook.def: A small script that runs automatically at certain moments, like before a command or after an edit.

subagent.def: A helper omp starts during a chat to work on part of the task in parallel.

checkpoint.def: A saved point in a chat that you can rewind to later.

tui.def: omp's own text interface in a terminal. visual-omp runs it for you in the background.

modelRole.def: Which AI model handles each job, such as everyday chat, planning or commit messages.

update.availableBody: The release notes list what changed.

notUpdatedBody.brew: The restart opened the previous copy. Run brew upgrade --cask visual-omp in Terminal to see what Homebrew reports.
notUpdatedBody.scoop: Scoop didn't install a newer version, and its PowerShell window shows what it reported. To try again, quit visual-omp, then run scoop update visual-omp in PowerShell, and open visual-omp when the command finishes.

check.hint: Check for new versions of visual-omp and omp.

dmg.stepsClosed: Open the disk image. Then quit visual-omp, drag visual-omp onto the Applications folder in its window and choose Replace, and open visual-omp again.
dmg.steps: The disk image is open in Finder. Quit visual-omp, drag visual-omp onto the Applications folder in that window and choose Replace, then open visual-omp again.

nsis.ready: Running the installer quits visual-omp so the installer can replace it.
nsis.starting: The installer is starting. visual-omp quits so the installer can replace it.

scoop.body: visual-omp closes, Scoop updates it in a PowerShell window, and visual-omp opens again when Scoop finishes.
scoop.global: Scoop installed this copy for all users, so only an administrator can update it, and visual-omp doesn't ask for administrator rights itself. Copy the command, quit visual-omp, run the command in PowerShell opened as an administrator, then open visual-omp again.

scoopSwitch.intro: Scoop can install visual-omp and update it without the installer.
scoopSwitch.install: Install Scoop if you don't have it, following the instructions on scoop.sh.
scoopSwitch.commands: In PowerShell, run these commands. The first installs Git, which Scoop needs to add the visual-omp bucket.
scoopSwitch.remove: Quit visual-omp and uninstall this copy in Windows Settings under Apps. Both copies use the same profile folder, so your chats and settings stay. Then open visual-omp from Scoop Apps in the Start menu.

omp.title: Update omp
omp.hint: Install the newest version of the omp engine.

omp.restarted_one: Restarted 1 chat on the new omp
omp.restarted_other: Restarted {{count}} chats on the new omp
omp.busyBody: When a reply finishes, use Restart omp in that chat's header.
